dedupe_keys.name: nairas nowcast of aerospace ionizing radiation system

description: NAIRAS is a physics-based model that predicts biologically hazardous radiation exposure of crew and passengers on aircraft or spacecraft from galactic cosmic rays, inner-belt trapped protons in low Earth orbit and solar energetic particles from solar eruptions. It couples models that transport cosmic radiation through the heliosphere, Earth's magnetosphere, the neutral atmosphere and aircraft or spacecraft shielding, driven by inputs such as GOES particle fluxes and neutron monitor data, and outputs dosimetric quantities such as absorbed dose in silicon and tissue and effective dose. It covers the globe: the real-time mode gives hourly maps on a 1 by 1 degree grid from the surface to 90 km in 1 km steps, operational at CCMC's iSWA since 2020, and the Runs-on-Request mode computes global doses for chosen periods or along uploaded aircraft, balloon or spacecraft trajectories. Version 4 adds high-resolution grids, pilot altitude maps and North Atlantic corridor plots with a 20 microsievert per hour contour, and a 2024 Space Weather paper by Phoenix, Mertens, Gronoff and Tobiska compares it with 45 flights from the ARMAS measurement inventory (2013 to 2023). Real-time products are available free on iSWA, and Runs-on-Request needs a CCMC user registration. Caveats: it is a research model and SEP forecasting from UMASEP is not yet used. It supports hazard exposure analysis and emergency response for aviation during solar storms; a related record is the FAA CARI-7 flight dose program.
